In the Calvin cycle, RuBisCO catalyzes the fixation reaction by combining CO2 with RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate), which has five carbon atoms [ev_003] [ev_007]. The resulting six-carbon compound is immediately broken down into two three-carbon compounds, 3-PGA [ev_007]. ATP and NADPH then use their stored energy to convert the three-carbon compound 3-PGA into another three-carbon compound, G3P, in a reduction reaction that involves the gain of electrons [ev_007] [ev_003].

Only one of the G3P molecules leaves the cycle, to contribute to the formation of a carbohydrate molecule such as glucose, and this requires six turns of the cycle to fix six carbon atoms [ev_001] [ev_002]. The remaining G3P molecules stay in the cycle and are used to regenerate RuBP, which prepares the system to fix more CO2 [ev_003] [ev_002]. Regeneration also uses ATP [ev_001] [ev_002]. The partial answer is limited to this source: the sources describe the export and regeneration roles, but they do not give a detailed mechanism for how the cycle chooses which G3P molecules leave.

In the Calvin cycle, RuBisCO catalyzes the fixation reaction by combining CO2 with RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate), which has five carbon atoms [ev_003] [ev_007]. The resulting six-carbon compound is immediately broken down into two three-carbon compounds, 3-PGA [ev_007]. ATP and NADPH then use their stored energy to convert the three-carbon compound 3-PGA into another three-carbon compound, G3P, in a reduction reaction that involves the gain of electrons [ev_007] [ev_003].

Only one of the G3P molecules leaves the cycle, to contribute to the formation of a carbohydrate molecule such as glucose, and this requires six turns of the cycle to fix six carbon atoms [ev_001] [ev_002]. The remaining G3P molecules stay in the cycle and are used to regenerate RuBP, which prepares the system to fix more CO2 [ev_003] [ev_002]. Regeneration also uses ATP [ev_001] [ev_002]. The partial answer is limited to this source: the sources describe the export and regeneration roles, but they do not give a detailed mechanism for how the cycle chooses which G3P molecules leave.
